title: The Coronavirus Explained & What You Should Do
beats: Timeline of outbreak, then asks what happens inside a human and what we should do
Virus as hull plus genes, not quite alive; admits surface survival is uncertain
Stowaway hitching a ride; journey to lungs
Epithelial cells as border cells; cell obeys instructions copy then self-destruct
Exponential growth: millions of cells and billions of viruses by day 10
Immune system turned into a weapon; cytokines as yelling, soldiers overdeployed
Neutrophils and killer T-cells as friendly-fire culprits
Most recover mild; severe share unknown but above flu
Escalation chain: lining lost, pneumonia, ventilator, sepsis
Flu comparison rejected; two futures, fast and slow
Why fast is bad: hospital overload, staff get sick, triage
Social vaccine = don't get infected, don't infect others
Soap melts the fat shell; wash like after jalapenos
Distancing and quarantine reframed as small price; you depend on others
Steep vs shallow slope decides ending; it is in our hands
Credits to Our World In Data

new_moves.name: scale-ladder
new_moves.what: Climb cell to tissue to patient to hospital to society in one causal chain

new_moves.name: stakes-before-advice
new_moves.what: Show the bad future so the boring behavior feels earned

theory: Advice lands because a mechanism chain was built first: cell obeys, immune system overreacts, hospitals overload, so behavior flattens the curve. Each rung is a causal why. The call to action is the last rung, not an appeal.
velocity: Orchestrator: for behavioral or policy topics, order mechanism scenes before action scenes and end with a callback to the hook
Scene builder: slope-comparison chart (fast vs slow) is the sim; let the learner drag the rate
Voice: tag uncertain facts with brief honest-caveat beats
quote: wash your hands as if you've just cut up some jalapeños
